subject: Pilot qualification: inference economics & constraints — next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Zhou <samantha@datadrive.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam@datadrive.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot qualification: inference economics & constraints — next steps

Hi Samantha / Liam,

Thanks for the 45 minute sync today — appreciate the transparency on where DataDrive.ai is seeing the sharpest cost pressure. Quick recap of what I captured and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Pain points you described
- Token unit economics are driving a freeze on feature expansion (high per-token cost at peak volumes).
- Current infra (self-hosted Triton endpoints + mixed GPU/CPU pools) struggles with tail latency during auction bursts.
- Engineering bandwidth is limited for deep model rework (quantize/rewire) — you prefer a server-side optimization partner vs full migration.

Current stack & constraints
- Models: in-house LLaMA-2 70B variants (some int8 experiments) served via Triton on GCP.
- Traffic: predictable baseline with 2x daily auction bursts (30-45 min) causing 3x CPU/GPU spend.
- Success criteria: P95 <= 500ms for low-latency endpoints; cost per 1M tokens < $X (we'll refine); no regression on completion quality vs baseline prompts.

Areas we discussed Redwood can help (initial):
1) Batching & KV-prefetch: automatic prefix batching and shared KV cache for repeated prompt patterns you mentioned (auctions).
2) Quantization strategy: evaluate safe quantization profiles (int8 / q4_0) per-model and measure quality delta on your eval set.
3) Routing/variant fallbacks: route lower-priority traffic to smaller quantized variants during bursts to keep high-priority SLA.
4) Cost model: a pilot cost model that projects unit economics given your burst profile + expected batching gains.

Immediate next steps (we agreed on these on the call)
- DataDrive: share the small eval set (50 canonical auction prompts) + one week of anonymized request headers/latency histogram (Liam will provide).
- Procurement: Samantha, loop in procurement for high-level terms — we will prepare a pilot SOW and a simple sizing estimate for review.
- Redwood: I'll send a short pilot proposal (technical scope + delta cost estimate) and a proposed 4-week timeline. Marissa (cc) will own the cost worksheet and baseline assumptions.

Attachments: I attached a one-page 'inference profile' template that would help us align on traffic and a draft MVP cost workbook (mvp_cost_v1.xlsx). Please fill/confirm the highlighted fields in the workbook.

Risks & ask
- If you are not open to evaluating quantized variants on a small sample, our projected savings can drop by ~30% — please confirm where you are on quantization experiments.
- We need the eval prompts + request histogram by EOD Thursday (16 Sep) to hit the pilot kickoff on Mon 21 Sep.

If that summary matches, I suggest a 30-minute check-in next Thursday to review the filled workbook before our internal sizing. Proposed times: 9am PT or 1pm PT.

Thanks again — great conversation.

--
Alex Martinez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Alex — thanks for the clear writeup. This aligns with what we heard internally. A few clarifications / confirmations: 

- We are willing to run a small quantization experiment (int8 + q4 variants) on the 50-prompt eval set you requested. Our main ask is that any degradation is measured against the exact scoring rubric our ML team uses — we'll attach that.
- We can provide the anonymized request histogram and 7 days of p50/p95/p99 latency from our Triton logs. Liam will drop those in the Drive folder by EOD Wednesday.
- Budget: we have a constrained pilot pool (cap of $25k for initial evaluation). If your pilot cost model requires more, please call that out and justify expected ROI — procurement will need the numbers.

Attachments: security_questionnaire.pdf (procurement wants it completed before any pilot contract).

Procurement note (Procurement): once we have the pilot SOW and the workbook from Redwood, we can do a fast-track PO process (Net 30) if terms are standard.

Samantha

Action items (who/when)
- Marissa: take the attached mvp_cost_v1.xlsx and produce a first-pass pilot cost worksheet (assumptions + projected token unit cost with/without batching & with conservative batching gains). Target: EOD Thu 16 Sep.
- Vivek: prepare a short technical note on quantization safety windows for LLaMA-2 70B (int8 vs q4 variants) and a lightweight test plan we can run against their 50-prompt eval. Target: Fri 17 Sep.
- Alex: I'll prepare the draft SOW and pilot scope doc (2-4 pages) — aim to share Mon 20 Sep.

Notes: prioritize conservative quality thresholds (we cannot accept a >2% drop in prompt pass rate on their rubric). If quantization is risky for their highest-value endpoints, propose per-route routing to smaller variants instead.

Let me know if the timelines conflict with other priorities.

--
